Definition: Ziph, the name of a place in Palestine; also of an Israelite
BiblicalUsage: Ziph is both a man and a place. The man is a son of Jehaleleel of Judah, named in the genealogies; the place is a town in the hill country of Judah, with a wilderness around it where David hid from Saul. The wilderness of Ziph is where David's trust was tested and where Saul hunted him and missed him.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Ziph shows how one name can carry two histories — a family's line and a fugitive's refuge — and both of them belong to the same story of God keeping David.
